strengths: QuEST addresses an important deployment problem with a practical design: teacher-generated calibration data, selective adaptation of fewer than 10% of parameters, and timestep-dependent activation quantization.

The W4A4 results demonstrate meaningful gains. On LSUN-Bedrooms and Churches, FID improves over EfficientDM from 10.60 to 5.64 and from 14.34 to 11.76, respectively. Stable Diffusion also produces recognizable images where the reported Q-Diffusion baseline fails.

Evaluation covers four models across unconditional, class-conditional, and text-to-image generation, generally using 50,000 images for LDM evaluation and 10,000 prompts for Stable Diffusion. The manuscript cites its datasets and baselines, provides a code link, and identifies relevant potential effects on watermarking and safety checking.

The sensitivity experiments provide useful motivation for selecting temporal and attention-related layers. Tables 6–7 support combining intermediate alignment with output supervision, and Table 7 demonstrates a concrete calibration-time improvement over Q-Diffusion.
weaknesses: The theoretical justification is unsound as written (Section 2.3.1 and Appendix B). Because the chosen MSE loss is quadratic in the final output, its second-order Taylor expansion with respect to that output is exact for any perturbation magnitude. Large perturbations therefore do not invalidate Equation 3 as claimed. Furthermore, Equation 5 replaces the small increment in Equation 10's Hessian quadratic with an output residual without justification. The derivation establishes neither the claimed sufficiency of fine-tuning nor sufficiency of the selected parameter subset.

The experiments insufficiently isolate the distinctive contribution. EfficientDM already provides data-free fine-tuning, and Appendix A acknowledges prior timestep grouping. Table 7 studies component additions only at W4A8 on LSUN-Bedrooms. Parameter-budget-matched layer-selection controls and joint-versus-progressive optimization comparisons at W4A4 are missing, leaving uncertainty about whether the headline gains specifically require the proposed selection and schedule.

Important quality tradeoffs remain insufficiently analyzed. On ImageNet at W4A4, IS falls from 364.73 for full precision to 202.45, versus 250.90 for EfficientDM; QuEST also has slightly worse sFID than EfficientDM despite lower FID. The manuscript itself questions FID in this setting, so these results require closer examination. Stable Diffusion evaluation relies solely on CLIPScore, which does not establish visual fidelity, while qualitative examples cover only two prompts.

The broader efficiency claims exceed the measurements. Table 7 shows approximately 34% less calibration time than Q-Diffusion but 20.5% more calibration memory. No corresponding resource comparison with EfficientDM or measured low-bit inference latency is provided. The headline 'full W4A4' terminology also needs qualification: first/last layers and attention operands retain 8-bit precision, and quantization targets the U-Net rather than the complete generation pipeline.

Despite the code link, the manuscript leaves important reproduction details unclear, including the exact selected layers for each architecture, batch size, guidance settings, and gradient treatment when fine-tuning quantized weights. There are also correctable reporting inconsistencies: Figure 5 highlights 25 timesteps while the text selects 20, and the LoRA comparison describes a 5.62 decrease in FID as evidence of worse performance.
